subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Holt <jason.holt@acme.com>, Linda Park <linda.park@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Hi Jason / Linda —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps. I bolded the items you asked us to confirm.

Summary of pain points and goals
- Primary pain: unpredictable inference latency for customer-facing chat, spikes during peak traffic causing inconsistent UX and costly overprovisioning.
- Goal: stabilize 95th-percentile latency to support a real-time chat experience while reducing average cost per 1M tokens.
- Target user-facing SLOs you stated: 95th pct first-byte latency <= 120 ms (US-west), tail latency budget for full response under 500 ms for typical 150–400 token responses.

Model & workload requirements
- Model family: mix of generation (assistant-style LLMs) for chat and embedding models for semantic search. You mentioned ~70% generation, 30% embedding in traffic distribution.
- Typical request size: 1–4 turns, average input length ~220 tokens, average output ~180 tokens. Peak QPS expected: 35–45 concurrent requests (chat sessions) during peak hour.

Deployment topology we discussed
- Preferred: Dedicated Redwood pool in us-west for primary traffic, with cross-region fallback to us-east for DR.
- KV/prefix caching at the edge for repeated prompts to reduce repeat compute.
- Quantization plan: start on int8-quantized variants for 16–32GB GPU footprints and scale to FP16 for high-quality per-response SLAs.

Action items (next steps)
1) We will produce an initial capacity estimate and cost projection (attached: acme-capacity-estimates.xlsx). ETA: Tue 6/23. (Vivek/Neha to own technical sizing.)
2) Neha will follow up with specific questions about token distribution and sample traffic. Please share a 1–2 day sample of anonymized traffic if possible.
3) If procurement is ready, I'll send a draft SOW and terms.

Attachments: acme-capacity-estimates.xlsx (draft), redwood-td-summary.pdf (high-level technical summary)

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up technical sync if you want a run-through of the sizing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Jason Holt <jason.holt@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few confirmations from our side:

- The 95th pct <=120 ms target is for first-byte across our US-west region only; for other regions a slightly higher target is acceptable.
- For tail/full-response SLA, 500 ms is a soft goal; worst-case allow 750 ms for larger generation tasks.
- We can provide an anonymized 48-hour traffic dump (JSON lines) — I'll have Linda share that with Neha.

On procurement: looping in procurement@acme.com — Linda is our PM and will coordinate the SOW and security questionnaire.

Next available for a focused technical sync is Thu 6/24 10:00–11:00 PT.

Thanks,
Jason
Head of Product, Acme Corp
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Holt <jason.holt@acme.com>, Linda Park <linda.park@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 12:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Hi Jason / Linda —

Thanks — appreciate you sending the traffic sample. A couple of quick technical clarifications to make sure our capacity estimate aligns with your needs:

1) Distribution: can you confirm the 70/30 generation vs embedding split across peak? If embeddings are batched, that will materially lower cost and GPU count.
2) Model baseline: do you have a preferred model family (e.g., Llama-2-70B-instruct / Mistral-like) or are you open to Redwood-recommended variants? We typically recommend starting with a quantized 13B–33B for predictable latency and evaluating quality regressions via your eval set.
3) Cold-starts & cache-warmup: do you expect significant variation in active sessions by user segment (e.g., 10% of users generate 60% of requests)? If so, we'll propose a warm pool strategy to reduce cold KV miss penalties.

Operational ask: please share the traffic dump link and a sample of your typical prompt templates. You can upload to the Drive link below or share via secure S3.

Drive upload: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d-acme-td

I'll take the traffic sample and produce two sizing options: (A) low-latency optimized (higher GPU count, smaller quantization delta) and (B) cost-optimized (larger quantization, batching). Deliverable ETA: Tue 6/23 EOD.

—Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Linda Park <linda.park@acme.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jason Holt <jason.holt@acme.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Thanks everyone — attaching the anonymized 48-hour traffic dump and a simple network diagram showing our current edge setup (attachment: network-diagram.png).

Answers inline:
- Confirmed: 70% generation / 30% embedding at peak. Embeddings are currently batched in-house but we can switch to Redwood batching if helpful.
- Model preference: open to recommendations. Prioritizing user-perceived latency; quality is important but we can iterate models after we stabilize latency.
- User skew: yes — roughly 15% of customers account for ~65% of peak requests.

We'll plan for the technical sync on Thu 6/24 10:00 PT. Procurement will review the draft SOW once you send it.

-Linda
Director, Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
attachments: network-diagram.png, acme-traffic-48h.jsonl
